title: Federal Criminal Arraignment Brief (US)
description: Skeleton defense brief for arraignment in federal district court addressing bail, discovery, and initial pleas.
body:
# FEDERAL CRIMINAL ARRAIGNMENT BRIEF

UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE [DISTRICT]

United States of America v. [DEFENDANT NAME]
Case No. [CASE NO.]

## I. Procedural posture
[Indictment/superseding indictment date; charges; prior appearances.]

## II. Bail / pretrial release
Under 18 U.S.C. § 3142 and the Bail Reform Act, the Government [does / does not] seek detention. The defense requests release on personal recognizance or unsecured bond because:
1. The defendant is not a flight risk: [community ties, employment, family].
2. The defendant poses no danger: [no violence, compliance history].
3. Proposed conditions: [GPS, third-party custodian, passport surrender, drug testing if applicable].

## III. Discovery and Brady
The defense requests immediate disclosure of Brady/Giglio material, Rule 16 discovery, and any § 851 enhancement notices.

## IV. Preservation and litigation hold
The defense requests preservation of [body-worn video, CART reports, 302s, business records] and a litigation hold to the investigating agency and USAO.

## V. Initial scheduling
The defense requests adequate time to review discovery before any trial date or dispositive motion deadline.

Respectfully submitted,
[DEFENSE COUNSEL]

**Drafting notes:**
- Confirm the correct federal district, magistrate judge assignment, and any local criminal rules.
- Research pretrial detention presumptions for the charged offenses (e.g., § 3142(e) drug/firearms presumptions).
- Calendar speedy trial (Speedy Trial Act) and initial conference deadlines immediately after arraignment.
- Request a written record of all proposed conditions and ensure the client understands compliance obligations.

title: Federal Sentencing Memorandum Checklist (US)
description: Checklist for preparing a sentencing memorandum and variance arguments under the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines.
body:
# Federal Sentencing Memorandum Checklist

- [ ] Obtain and review the Presentence Investigation Report (PSR) and all addenda; file timely objections to factual errors and guideline calculations
- [ ] Calculate the advisory Guidelines range (Ch. 2 offense level + Ch. 3 adjustments + Ch. 4 criminal history); verify grouping, relevant conduct, and loss/drug quantity tables
- [ ] Identify applicable policy statements (e.g., §5K2.0 for substantial assistance, §5H1.11 for family ties) and circuit precedent on variances after *Booker*
- [ ] Compile mitigation: employment history, community service, mental health/substance treatment, restitution capacity, acceptance of responsibility
- [ ] Gather character letters (employers, clergy, family) with counsel cover letter explaining relevance under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a)
- [ ] Address mandatory minimums, § 924(c) stacking, and any 18 U.S.C. § 3553(f) safety valve eligibility
- [ ] Propose a concrete sentence (probation, home confinement, RDAP eligibility) and location/BOP designation factors
- [ ] Prepare a sentencing hearing outline and exhibits; confirm whether the court permits live witnesses or letter-only mitigation
- [ ] File the memorandum within the court's deadline (often 7–14 days before sentencing) and serve the Government
- [ ] Calendar appeal waiver scope (if any), restitution/judgment dates, and supervised release conditions

**Practical notes:**
- Object to PSR errors in writing; many courts treat unobjected facts as admitted.
- Anchor variance arguments in § 3553(a) factors, not merely disagreement with the Guidelines.
- Confirm whether the plea agreement's appeal waiver covers the sentence sought.

title: Civil Complaint — Breach of Contract (California)
description: State court complaint skeleton for breach of written contract under California law with prayer for damages.
body:
# COMPLAINT FOR BREACH OF CONTRACT

SUPERIOR COURT OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF [COUNTY]

[PLAINTIFF NAME], Plaintiff,
v.
[DEFENDANT NAME], Defendant.
Case No. __________

## COMPLAINT FOR BREACH OF CONTRACT

Plaintiff [PLAINTIFF] alleges:

1. **Parties.** Plaintiff is [description]. Defendant is [description] and may be served at [address].
2. **Jurisdiction and venue.** This Court has jurisdiction under Cal. Civ. Proc. Code §§ 410.10, 395; venue is proper in [COUNTY] because [contract performance / injury occurred here].
3. **Contract.** On or about [DATE], the parties entered a [WRITTEN/ORAL] agreement (the "Agreement") [attach or describe].
4. **Plaintiff's performance.** Plaintiff performed all conditions precedent, or was excused from performance because [reason].
5. **Defendant's breach.** Defendant breached the Agreement by [failure to pay / deliver / perform] on or about [DATE], in violation of Section [X].
6. **Damages.** As a direct and proximate result, Plaintiff has suffered damages in an amount not less than $[AMOUNT], plus interest, costs, and attorney's fees if recoverable under [Agreement § / statute].

## PRAYER FOR RELIEF
Plaintiff requests: (1) compensatory damages; (2) pre- and post-judgment interest; (3) costs of suit; (4) such other relief as the Court deems just.

Dated: [DATE]
[ATTORNEY / PLAINTIFF]

**Drafting notes:**
- Plead the contract with specificity (written vs. oral; integration clause if suing on the written instrument).
- Allege performance or excuse and connect breach to ascertainable damages; avoid conclusory loss statements.
- Check arbitration/forum-selection clauses before filing; consider demurrer risks on pleading defects.
- Verify statute of limitations (written contract: 4 years; oral: 2 years) and any attorney-fee provision.

title: Federal Civil Discovery Plan Checklist (US)
description: Checklist for preparing a Rule 26(f) conference report and discovery plan in federal civil litigation.
body:
# Federal Civil Discovery Plan Checklist

- [ ] Review Local Rules and individual judge's discovery order (page limits, ESI protocol, subpoena practice)
- [ ] Prepare Rule 26(f) conference agenda: jurisdiction, preserved claims/defenses, settlement posture, initial disclosures (Rule 26(a)(1))
- [ ] Exchange initial disclosures on time; include witnesses, documents, damages computation, and insurance
- [ ] Draft discovery plan: fact and expert discovery deadlines, motion cutoff, and trial date assumptions
- [ ] Plan interrogatories (Rule 33), document requests (Rule 34), and admissions (Rule 36) sequences; set internal response calendars (30-day default)
- [ ] Address ESI: sources, custodians, search terms, format, clawback under Rule 26(b)(5), and preservation holds
- [ ] Schedule depositions (Rule 30): party and expert (Rule 26(b)(4)) with 7-hour presumptive limit unless stipulated or ordered
- [ ] Identify discovery disputes for early conferral; prepare Rule 37 meet-and-confer letters before motion
- [ ] Calendar expert disclosures (Rule 26(a)(2)) and rebuttal deadlines
- [ ] File the Rule 26(f) report and proposed scheduling order promptly after the conference

**Practical notes:**
- Treat the scheduling order as a hard contract — missed deadlines often require leave of court.
- Build a litigation hold at case inception and document custodians and data sources.
- Coordinate damages discovery with expert retention and Daubert risk early.

title: Section 1983 Civil Rights Complaint (US)
description: Federal complaint skeleton alleging deprivation of constitutional rights under 42 U.S.C. § 1983.
body:
# COMPLAINT — 42 U.S.C. § 1983

UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE [DISTRICT]

[PLAINTIFF NAME], Plaintiff,
v.
[DEFENDANT OFFICIALS / ENTITY], Defendants.
Case No. __________

## COMPLAINT FOR VIOLATION OF CIVIL RIGHTS (42 U.S.C. § 1983)

Plaintiff alleges:

1. **Jurisdiction.** This Court has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331 and 1343; supplemental state-law claims under § 1367.
2. **Parties.** Plaintiff is [description]. Defendants are [state actors / municipal entity] acting under color of state law.
3. **Facts.** On [DATE], at [LOCATION], Defendants [describe conduct: arrest, use of force, retaliation, denial of process].
4. **Constitutional violation.** Defendants violated Plaintiff's rights under the [Fourth/Fourth and Fourteenth] Amendment by [unreasonable seizure / excessive force / procedural due process], as established by [clearly established law at the time].
5. **Municipal liability (Monell).** [ENTITY] maintained a policy, custom, or failure-to-train that caused the violation; [plead pattern or final policymaker act].
6. **Damages.** Plaintiff suffered [physical injury, medical expenses, lost wages, emotional distress] and seeks compensatory and punitive damages where permitted.

## PRAYER FOR RELIEF
Compensatory damages, declaratory and injunctive relief, attorney's fees under 42 U.S.C. § 1988, costs, and jury trial demanded.

**Drafting notes:**
- Plead each defendant's personal involvement; respondeat superior does not apply to individuals.
- For municipalities, plead Monell policy/custom with specificity — not merely respondeat superior.
- Check qualified immunity framing; allege clearly established law with factual particularity.
- Review abstention, Eleventh Amendment, and statute of limitations (state borrowing doctrine).

title: Master Software License Agreement (US)
description: Enterprise software license agreement skeleton with limitation of liability, IP, and data security terms.
body:
# MASTER SOFTWARE LICENSE AGREEMENT

This Master Software License Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of [DATE] by and between [LICENSOR], a [STATE] [entity type] ("Licensor"), and [LICENSEE] ("Licensee").

1. **License grant.** Licensor grants Licensee a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use the Software and Documentation for Licensee's internal business purposes during the Term, subject to the Usage Metrics in Exhibit A.
2. **Restrictions.** Licensee shall not reverse engineer, sublicense, or use the Software to build a competing product except as permitted by applicable law.
3. **Fees and payment.** Licensee shall pay fees per Exhibit B; late payments accrue interest at [1.5]% per month or the maximum lawful rate.
4. **Support and SLA.** Licensor shall provide support per Exhibit C; service credits are Licensee's sole remedy for SLA failures unless otherwise stated.
5. **Data and security.** Licensor shall maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards consistent with [SOC 2 / industry standards]; data processing terms are in Exhibit D.
6. **IP ownership.** Licensor retains all right, title, and interest in the Software; Licensee owns its data and grants Licensor a limited license to process it to perform the Services.
7. **Warranty disclaimer.** THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS" EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN SECTION 8.
8. **Express warranty.** Licensor warrants that the Software will materially conform to the Documentation for [90] days; exclusive remedy is repair/replace or refund of prepaid fees.
9. **Indemnification.** Each party shall defend the other against third-party claims arising from [IP infringement / Licensee data violations] subject to prompt notice and control.
10. **Limitation of liability.** NEITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY EXCEEDS FEES PAID IN THE TWELVE MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM; NO INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES EXCEPT FOR [CONFIDENTIALITY BREACH / INDEMNITY OBLIGATIONS].
11. **Term and termination.** Either party may terminate for material breach uncured within [30] days; upon termination Licensee shall cease use and certify deletion.
12. **Governing law.** [STATE] law governs; exclusive venue in [COUNTY, STATE] courts or federal courts therein.

**Drafting notes:**
- Align usage metrics, deployment model (on-prem vs. SaaS), and support tiers in exhibits.
- Negotiate liability caps, super-caps for data breach, and carve-outs for IP indemnity and confidentiality.
- Confirm export control, open-source, and audit rights match the client's compliance posture.

title: Consumer Complaint Response Letter (US)
description: Business response template to a consumer complaint escalated to a regulator or BBB with investigation hold language.
body:
# CONSUMER COMPLAINT RESPONSE

[COMPANY LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

[REGULATOR / BBB / AG OFFICE]
Re: Consumer Complaint No. [ID] — [CONSUMER NAME]

Dear [OFFICER]:

[COMPANY] received your notice regarding the above complaint. We take consumer concerns seriously and have investigated the matter.

1. **Account summary.** [Product/service, purchase date, account or order number.]
2. **Investigation.** We reviewed [billing records, service logs, correspondence dated [DATES]].
3. **Position.** [Acknowledge error and describe cure] OR [Explain why the charge/service was proper with citation to terms of service / contract provision].
4. **Resolution offered.** We have [issued refund of $X / provided replacement / extended service] and notified the consumer on [DATE].
5. **Preventive action.** We have [updated training / revised disclosures / corrected billing code] to reduce recurrence.

Please contact [NAME, TITLE, PHONE, EMAIL] with further questions. This response is provided without admission of liability where disputes remain contested.

Sincerely,
[AUTHORIZED SIGNATORY]

**Drafting notes:**
- Respond within the regulator's deadline; preserve documents under a short litigation hold.
- Avoid admitting liability if litigation is reasonably anticipated; describe corrective action factually.
- Ensure the response matches actual account records and prior consumer communications.
- Route through consumer compliance and, if material, in-house counsel before submission.

title: Secured Promissory Note (US)
description: Promissory note with security interest grant cross-referencing a UCC-1 collateral description.
body:
# SECURED PROMISSORY NOTE

$[PRINCIPAL AMOUNT] | [CITY, STATE] | [DATE]

FOR VALUE RECEIVED, [BORROWER] ("Borrower") promises to pay [LENDER] ("Lender") the principal sum of [AMOUNT] together with interest at [RATE]% per annum, with payments as follows: [AMORTIZATION / INTEREST-ONLY / BALLOON ON [DATE]].

1. **Maturity.** All unpaid principal and accrued interest is due on [MATURITY DATE] ("Maturity").
2. **Default.** Events of default include: (a) payment failure continuing [10] days; (b) breach of the Security Agreement; (c) insolvency; (d) material misrepresentation. Upon default, Lender may accelerate and pursue remedies under the Security Agreement and UCC Article 9.
3. **Security.** This Note is secured by the Collateral described in the Security Agreement dated [DATE] and UCC financing statement to be filed in [JURISDICTION].
4. **Prepayment.** Borrower may prepay without penalty / with [YIELD MAINTENANCE] as stated in Exhibit A.
5. **Governing law.** This Note is governed by [STATE] law without regard to conflicts principles.
6. **Notices.** Notices to the addresses in the Security Agreement; email permitted if acknowledged.

BORROWER: ____________________
LENDER: ____________________

**Drafting notes:**
- Cross-reference a Security Agreement with a collateral description broad enough for the transaction (accounts, equipment, IP as permitted).
- Confirm usury limits, licensed-lender requirements, and whether the loan is consumer or commercial.
- Calendar UCC-1 filing, continuation, and fixture filing if real property is collateral.
- Align default interest, attorney's fees, and choice-of-law with the credit agreement suite.

title: UCC Article 9 Foreclosure Timeline Checklist (US)
description: Checklist for conducting a UCC Article 9 private sale or disposition of collateral after default.
body:
# UCC Article 9 Foreclosure Checklist

- [ ] Confirm perfected security interest: UCC-1 on file, priority search, no intervening liens requiring subordination
- [ ] Review loan documents for default, notice addresses, and cure periods; document the default trigger event
- [ ] Send commercially reasonable default notice identifying secured obligations and intended disposition method (private sale vs. public auction)
- [ ] Provide debtor and guarantor the opportunity to cure if required by agreement or state law overlay
- [ ] Obtain updated collateral valuation (appraisal, blue book, market quotes) to support commercial reasonableness
- [ ] Select disposition method: private sale to qualified buyer vs. public sale; avoid purchase by secured party unless permitted after commercially reasonable notice
- [ ] Send disposition notice with time, place, and manner sufficient for interested parties to attend or bid
- [ ] Apply sale proceeds: reasonable expenses of retaking, holding, preparing, and selling, then to secured obligation; account for surplus or deficiency
- [ ] Prepare a disposition affidavit and buyer bill of sale; release liens on any retained collateral
- [ ] Send deficiency or surplus letter to debtor and any secondary obligor; calendar any anti-deficiency or notice statutes

**Practical notes:**
- Commercial reasonableness of method, manner, time, place, and terms is the central UCC test.
- Do not sell collateral to an insider secured party without strict compliance with § 9-610 restrictions.
- Preserve notices, valuations, and bidding records for later deficiency litigation.

title: AAA Commercial Arbitration Demand (US)
description: Demand for arbitration under AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules with statement of claim outline.
body:
# DEMAND FOR ARBITRATION (AAA COMMERCIAL RULES)

TO: [RESPONDENT NAME AND ADDRESS]
CC: American Arbitration Association, [REGIONAL OFFICE]

Re: Demand for Arbitration — [CONTRACT NAME] dated [DATE]

Claimant [CLAIMANT] hereby demands arbitration before the AAA under the Commercial Arbitration Rules.

1. **Agreement to arbitrate.** The parties' [MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT / PURCHASE AGREEMENT] contains an arbitration clause at Section [X] requiring binding AAA arbitration in [CITY, STATE].
2. **Brief statement of claim.** [Chronology of dispute; breach or non-payment; damages sought $[AMOUNT].]
3. **Relief sought.** Claimant seeks [damages, specific performance, attorney's fees, interest, costs].
4. **Hearing locale.** Claimant proposes [CITY, STATE] per the contract seat/venue clause.
5. **Arbitrator request.** [Single arbitrator / three arbitrators] with [industry / legal] background.
6. **Filing fee.** Enclosed is the AAA filing fee of $[AMOUNT] [or request fee allocation per rules/contract].

Claimant reserves the right to amend the statement of claim. Please serve a response within the time required by the Rules.

[CLAIMANT COUNSEL]

**Drafting notes:**
- Attach the arbitration agreement and confirm AAA vs. JAMS vs. ad hoc rules referenced in the contract.
- Check for prior mediation prerequisites, fee-splitting, and limitations on punitive or consequential damages.
- Calendar answer/counterclaim deadlines under the selected rules and request a preliminary management conference if available.

title: Arbitration Hearing Preparation Checklist (US)
description: Checklist for preparing witnesses, exhibits, and hearing briefs for a commercial arbitration hearing.
body:
# Arbitration Hearing Preparation Checklist

- [ ] Confirm panel appointment, conflict disclosures, and preliminary order governing briefing schedule and exhibit exchange
- [ ] Finalize exhibit list with Bates ranges; prepare hearing binders (chronology, key contracts, damages model)
- [ ] Prepare direct examinations and cross outlines; conduct mock Q&A for fact and expert witnesses
- [ ] Exchange expert reports/rebuttals per the scheduling order; prepare expert stipulations where possible
- [ ] Draft opening statement themes: liability, causation, damages, and credibility contrasts
- [ ] Prepare demonstratives (timelines, org charts) and seek panel approval for oversized exhibits or electronics
- [ ] File any pending dispositive or bifurcation motions; prepare a hearing brief with table of authorities
- [ ] Coordinate subpoenas for third-party documents or attendance if permitted by forum rules
- [ ] Prepare a closing outline linking testimony and exhibits to requested relief
- [ ] Calendar post-hearing briefing deadlines and form of award (reasoned vs. standard)

**Practical notes:**
- Arbitration discovery is typically narrower — prioritize the documents that will be offered at hearing.
- Agree exhibit foundations early to avoid wasting hearing time on authentication disputes.
- Confirm whether the panel will hear attorney's fees and interest in the same phase or bifurcate.

title: Chapter 11 Voluntary Petition Skeleton (US)
description: Skeleton outline for preparing a Chapter 11 voluntary petition and first-day motions.
body:
# CHAPTER 11 VOLUNTARY PETITION — PREPARATION OUTLINE

Debtor: [LEGAL NAME]
EIN: [EIN]
Principal place of business: [ADDRESS]

## Voluntary petition package
- Official Form 201 (Voluntary Petition for Non-Individuals)
- List of creditors (Excel per court format) with top 20 unsecured creditors highlighted
- Schedules A/B–J and Statement of Financial Affairs (SOFA) with insider and preference windows
- Corporate ownership statement (Rule 1007(b)) and petitioning affiliate matrix if part of a group filing

## First-day motions (drafting list)
1. **Cash collateral / DIP financing** — budget, roll-ups, priming analysis, adequate protection
2. **Wages and benefits** — pay pre-petition wages/benefits within court-approved caps
3. **Utilities** — adequate assurance under § 366
4. **Insurance** — maintain policies; pay premiums
5. **Claims and noticing agent** — Kroll/Epiq appointment and 341 calendar
6. **Critical vendors** (if used in jurisdiction) — necessity and harm standard

## Corporate authority
- Board resolutions authorizing filing, retention of counsel, and DIP terms
- Certificate of counsel regarding good-faith filing and cash collateral negotiations

**Drafting notes:**
- Confirm venue under § 1408 and whether a prepack/prearranged plan strategy applies.
- Build 13-week cash flow and variance reporting before first-day hearing.
- Coordinate UCC outreach, RSA/APA timelines, and stay violation outreach to secured lenders.
